title: refactor(app-shell): Studio's access panels pick with the shared Select (objectui#11865)
body:
Part of #11865
Clause-②: no

The access panels slice of objectui#11865 (claim 6066038274): the four browser-native select elements in Studio's Access pillar become the shared Radix `Select`. Two are in the package OWD overview (each row's internal and external sharing model). Two are in a permission set's advanced facets (an RLS policy's operation and a tab's visibility). The card stays open for the other native selects. The earlier slices are objectui#11934 (the Group panel), objectui#11976 (the validation editor), objectui#11990 (*Explain access*) and objectui#11995 (object settings).

## What changed

- `packages/app-shell/src/views/studio-design/PackageOwdOverviewPanel.tsx`: one module-private `OwdPicker`, drawn with the shared `Select` from `@object-ui/components`, renders both dials of every row. It follows object settings' `SettingsPicker`. Items carry their option's index, so the "not set" options, whose value is `''`, need no empty `SelectItem`. A stored value that none of the options carries gets an item of its own. Each pick hands the option's own value to the same `setEdit` call the native `onChange` made. The triggers keep the native controls' test ids (`owd-internal-` and `owd-external-` plus the object name). A wider external dial still wears the amber border. Read-only still draws no dial: the row shows the value's label, as before.
- `packages/app-shell/src/views/metadata-admin/PermissionAdvancedFacets.tsx`: one module-private `FacetPicker`, built the same way, renders the RLS operation and the tab visibility. Each caller's update is the native `onChange` body, with the event's value replaced by the picked value. Read-only passes `disabled` to the primitive (objectui#11781). The triggers gain test ids: `rls-operation-` plus the policy index, and `tab-visibility-` plus the tab key. The now-unused `selectCls` constant is gone.
- Untouched: every other control in both panels, the props, the exports and the write paths. No i18n key is added: each panel's set of `engine.*` / `perm.*` keys is identical to the base's (diffed).
- New pins: `PackageOwdOverviewPanel.sharedSelect-11865.test.tsx` (17 tests) and `PermissionAdvancedFacets.sharedSelect-11865.test.tsx` (22 tests).
- Eight suites drove the native controls with a `change` event or read the native select's `value`. They now open the trigger and pick, and read the trigger's text:
  - `PackageOwdOverviewPanel.test.tsx`, `.layersUnsaved-11799`, `.picklistServedOptions-11692`, `.readDecorationStrip` and `.servedDraftTakenAsIs-10765`;
  - `StudioDesignSurface.accessGuard.test.tsx` and `StudioDesignSurface.pillarNavGuard.test.tsx`, which mount the real overview through the Access pillar;
  - `PermissionMatrixEditor.packageDoorFacets.test.tsx`, which authors a tab's visibility through the real facets.

  Three of the `value` reads expected `''`: the 11799 CONTROL case, the 10765 list-load case, and the access guard's reload. A button's `value` is `''` whatever it shows, so those three would have passed vacuously. They now assert the "not set" label as the trigger's text.
- `.changeset/11865-access-panels-shared-select.md`: `@object-ui/app-shell: patch`.

## Hypotheses

- **H1, value parity: held.** A scratch probe (uncommitted, deleted) fired a `change` event on every option of each native select on base `b13ea3c67`, then recorded the write. For the overview, that is the object draft Save sent. For the facets, it is the draft the `setDraft` updater produced. A second probe picked the same options through the triggers on head. The two readings are identical for all 9 overview rows and for 11 of the 14 facet rows. The other 3 are the re-pick rows (the option already shown):
  - on base, jsdom's `change` event fired for them and wrote the draft again;
  - for a policy with no operation, which shows "all", that write added `operation: 'all'`;
  - on head, a re-pick writes nothing, which is what a browser does for an option that is already selected.

  So the re-pick rows pin the primitive, not a browser reading of the native control. The overview's re-pick rows were already no-writes on base (the row stays clean, Save stays disabled), and they are on head too. The new suites pin every option against those literals as JSON text, plus a table-coverage test of each picker's listed options in order.
- **H2, labels, keyboard and read-only: held, with one panel that has no read-only control.** None of the four native selects had an accessible name: no label, no `aria-label`. The probe read `''` for each. The triggers have none either, which is pinned. Enter opens a picker, and Enter on an option selects it.
  - The facets have a read-only state, `writable: false`. In it, each trigger is disabled, wears the primitive's own `disabled:` classes, and does not open.
  - The overview's read-only state draws no control at all, on base and on head: each row shows its values as text. That is pinned as it stands. Turning it into a disabled trigger would be a change beyond the control swap.
- **H3, a stored value outside the options: held.** Each of these is shown in its trigger and listed first, and re-picking it writes nothing: a sharing model neither dial offers (`full`, `read_write`), an RLS operation the picker does not list (`read`), and a tab visibility it does not list (`default`). The native controls showed their first option there ("not set", "all", "Visible").
- **H4, first-load bytes: falsified for the facets, held for the overview.** Measured on `703fb048c` with `apps/console` `vite build` plus `node scripts/check-eager-closure-budget.mjs`. The two legs are head, and the same tree with both panels at their base blobs (landing and restore proven by hash).
  - Head: `Console eager closure is 3311.6 KB gzipped across 337 of 2459 chunks (budget: 3312.0 KB, headroom: 0.4 KB).`
  - Base: `Console eager closure is 3311.4 KB gzipped across 337 of 2459 chunks (budget: 3312.0 KB, headroom: 0.6 KB).`
  - `eagerGzipBytes` 3390870 to 3391092 (+222), and `eagerRawBytes` +349. The facets ship in the eager `src` chunk, which grows by 349 raw and 211 gzipped bytes; that is `FacetPicker`. The entry chunk's bytes are identical, but its gzip is 11 bytes larger, because the `src` chunk's hashed name inside it changed.
  - The overview ships in the lazy `studioBuilder` chunk and adds no eager bytes.

  The budget bot's reading on this PR is the authority.

## Reverse leg

With the implementation committed, both panels were written from their base blobs. The hashes equal the base blobs, with 2 native select elements in each panel and no picker. Then the two new suites and the eight converted suites ran: `56 failed, 18 passed (74)`, vitest exit 1.
- Red: all 22 facet pins; 14 of the 17 overview pins; and every converted case (6 in `PackageOwdOverviewPanel.test.tsx`, 3 in 11799, 2 in 11692, 1 in `readDecorationStrip`, 2 in 10765, 3 in `accessGuard`, 1 in `pillarNavGuard`, 2 in `packageDoorFacets`).
- Green: the overview suite's two read-only cases and its name pin, which hold on both because the native dials had no name either; and the untouched cases of the converted suites.

That is the direction the suite headers state. The restore, `git checkout HEAD --` under a trap, is proven: both hashes equal the HEAD blobs, and `git diff HEAD` is 0 bytes. The panels are imported by relative path in every suite, so no `dist` was involved.

## Gates (on `703fb048c`)

- 35 suites, repo-root `pnpm exec vitest run`: `Test Files 35 passed (35)`, `Tests 219 passed (219)`. They are the suites a `git grep` finds mounting the real overview or the real facets: the two panels' own suites, every `PermissionMatrixEditor.*` suite, the CEL suites that mount the facets, and the four `StudioDesignSurface` suites that mount the Access pillar.
- `column-identity.ratchet` and `one-authority-per-exported-name-6273`: `Test Files 2 passed (2)`, `Tests 18 passed (18)`.
- `pnpm --filter @object-ui/app-shell type-check`, after the app-shell dependency closure build: exit 0. By `--listFilesOnly`, both panels are in the main program, and all 12 touched `.tsx` files are in the test program.
- `pnpm exec eslint` on the 12 touched `.tsx` files: exit 0, 0 errors, 20 warnings. All 20 are on base: each modified file's rule list is identical to its base blob's, read through `--stdin`. The two new suites have none.
- `check-changeset-presence`, `check-changeset-no-major`, `check:new-line-citations` (0 new) and `check:control-bytes`: exit 0.
- Also exit 0: the changeset fixed, overwrite and claims gates, `pending-changeset-literals`, `test-path-roots`, the three vi-mock gates, `phantom-deps`, `unreferenced-sources`, `i18n-keys`, `i18n-designer-parity`, `i18n-drift`, `metadata-write-doors`, `esm-specifiers`, `self-import`, lint coverage, type-check coverage, `handler-key-reads` and `designer-field-key-parity`. `component-surface-parity` and `i18n-dead-keys` also exit 0; both are report-only.
- Declared to CI: the full `pnpm test` farm and repo-wide `pnpm lint`.

## Acceptance notes

- None of the four pickers has an accessible name, on base or on head, because this slice keeps each control's name as it was. In the overview the column headers name the dials visually; in the facets nothing does. Naming them would need an aria-label. Noted, not filed.
- The overview's read-only state shows text, not a disabled trigger, as on base. Triage's "the read-only state follows the primitive" applies to the facets, whose native controls were disabled.
- First-load bytes: +222 gzipped bytes on the eager closure, all from the facets (see H4).
- Browser: not measured in this slice. Keyboard and read-only behaviour are pinned in the test DOM only.
